div.p: The diagnosis and treatment of gliomas depend greatly on the precise delineation of tumor boundaries and the rapid extraction of molecular pathological features. The development of high-resolution and high-sensitivity terahertz (THz) attenuated total reflection (ATR) imaging technology can greatly expand its application in the clinical medical field. In this study, we demonstrated a THz ATR imaging system based on a solid immersion lens (SIL). The resolution improvement mechanism by a solid immersion lens in the THz ATR imaging system has been studied theoretically and experimentally. According to the theoretical analysis results, the optimal parameters of the system have been selected. The spatial resolution of the THz imaging system was up to 120µm × 140µm. On this basis, the THz reflectivity of fresh normal brain tissue and glioma tissue in a mouse model was studied. Compared with the visible, MR, and H&E-stained images, the accurate identification of the glioma region boundary and microscopic structures in brain tissues was realized. The glioma regions in H&E-stained and THz ATR images were segmented automatically based on the Chan-Vese active contour model, where the performance evaluation rates were all above 95%. These promising results suggest that THz ATR imaging based on SIL could be used as a tool for label-free, high-sensitivity, and real-time imaging of brain gliomas.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Gliomas are intracranial tumors that mainly occur in the functional regions of the brain [1]. Due to the invasive growth of glioma and the highly malignant invasive damage to the functional regions of brain tissue, gliomas have a high rate of in situ recurrence and mortality. Therefore, the accurate delineation of the glioma region is one of the key factors for the targeted treatment based on the molecular pathological characteristics of the tumor, which could reduce the probability of tumor recurrence and improve the survival rate of patients. Neuroimaging method, such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), is the basic method of tumor localization clinically for its high sensitivity and specificity, which plays as a guidance role in making surgery plans and the evaluation of recovery in post-operation. However, this method has some limitations, such as time-consuming, high cost, inhomogeneous static magnetic field-induced distortion, and exposure to ionizing radiation [2]. Histopathologic examination, such as hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, can assess tumor grade by observing cell morphology and infiltration. It is used as the gold standard for the qualitative diagnosis of glioma in clinical practice. But it is limited to the analysis of ex vivo glioma tissue, and the results mostly are affected by the subjective assessment of pathologists [3]. At present, intraoperative MRI combined with neuronavigation and intraoperative pathological biopsy becomes the main clinical diagnostic method [4][5][6]. However, this approach has the disadvantages of expensive equipment and site construction, and increased operative time and surgical risks. Additionally, it is difficult to achieve perfect correspondence and mutual interpretation between microscopic pathology and macroscopic images due to the deviation in tumor location between MRI and pathological results. Therefore, there is still urgent demand to develop a rapid, high-sensitivity, and accurate detection method to assist glioma diagnosis.

Terahertz (THz) wave, located between microwave and infrared band, has attracted great attention in biological imaging due to its unique characteristics of high sensitivity to water, noninvasiveness, and nonionization [7]. At present, THz imaging has been widely applied in medical diagnostics, especially for the differentiation and localization between healthy tissues and malignant neoplasms of various diseases [8][9][10]. According to the imaging methods, THz imaging can be divided into transmission imaging, reflection imaging and attenuated total reflection (ATR) imaging. Basically, THz transmission imaging requires the tissue to be sliced due to the high absorption of water in fresh tissue. THz reflection imaging is frequently used for sample measurement with a quartz window covered considering the signal is easily affected by diffuse reflection for uneven surface of samples. Comparatively, THz ATR imaging can obtain more information on the interaction between the sample and the evanescent wave traveling along the ATR prism surface, which has high sensitivity and can ensure the integrity of samples [11]. Until now, THz ATR imaging has been used for in vivo and ex vivo glioma detection. Considering the secondary reflection and the small imaging area caused by the scanning mode, the imaging area of THz ATR imaging system is still limited by the design of ATR prism [12,13].

Considering the wavelength of THz wave is a few hundred micrometers, it imposes significant limitations on the spatial resolution of THz imaging in general. The high-accuracy delineation of the boundaries of malignant tumor is still restricted. Therefore, various THz imaging techniques with higher spatial resolution have been developed. THz near-field imaging technique [14] and the THz imaging system based on the terajet effect from dielectric structures [15,16] can overcome the diffraction limit and achieve higher resolution values up to 10 -2 λ to 10 -4 λ, but the limited working distance and the relatively weak signal intensity restrict their application in in vivo imaging. THz digital holography [17] and the synthesis aperture imaging method [18] can also achieve sub-wavelength spatial resolution, but they require complex computations to resolve the inverse ill-posed problems and reconstruct THz images. Solid immersion lens (SIL) with high refractive index and high THz transmittance can effectively increase the refractive index of the object space [19]. Thereby, the imaging resolution can be significantly enhanced with the improved numerical aperture (NA) of the imaging system. At present, the full-field THz imaging system based on SIL has been developed with sub-wavelength resolution [20]. However, it was difficult to obtain high contrast images of biological tissues based on this imaging system, especially for the in vivo biological samples. The reflection-mode THz solid immersion microscope system with the resolution of less than 0.15λ has been reported based on a wide-aperture aspherical singlet and a hemispherical SIL [21][22][23][24]. The identification of the heterogeneity in ex vivo glioma brain tissue was realized with the resolution of 75µm. Compared with reflection mode, ATR imaging mode can provide higher contrast and sensitivity, which is more suitable for the detection of the in vivo biological tissues. However, the THz ATR imaging system based on SIL with high resolution and high sensitivity has not been reported.

In this paper, a novel arrangement of the continuous-wave (CW) THz ATR imaging system based on SIL (THz SIL-ATR) was proposed. A separated hyper-hemispherical SIL made of high-resistivity float-zone silicon (HRFZ-Si) was designed to realize THz SIL-ATR imaging with unrestricted imaging area, where the SIL was comprised of a truncated hemispherical lens and an imaging window. The imaging resolution improvement of hyper-hemispherical SIL was analyzed by the finite-element frequency-domain method. And the influence of air gap thickness between the truncated hemispherical lens and imaging window on the THz transmittance under different polarizations was analyzed theoretically. The imaging resolution of the system was 120 µm × 140 µm. The THz imaging of water drop with large area of 25.5 × 23.0 mm 2 has been demonstrated with high sensitivity and stability. Furthermore, THz imaging of freshly excised normal and glioma tissues has been performed. The various microscopic structures, such as hippocampus and lobule of cerebellar vermis in normal mouse brain tissues, can be accurately identified for their different reflectivity of THz wave. The glioma regions in THz images can be corresponded well to the H&E-stained images using the automatic segmentation method based on the Chan-Vese active contour model, where the average accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score were up to 95.25%, 95.47%, 95.04%, 95.45%, and 95.26%. The results indicated that THz ATR imaging based on SIL has great potential in the label-free diagnosis of brain gliomas.

div.head: Sample preparation
div.p: A reproducible measurement protocol was established by standardizing all experimental steps of sample preparations and THz measurements. Five-week-old male nude mice in weight from 20-22 g were purchased from the Department of Neurosurgery, Southwest Hospital (Chongqing, China). All animal experiments in this work were performed in accordance with the China Animal Welfare Legislation, and were approved by the Third Military Medical University.

The glioma model was established by implanting U87 MG glioma cells into nude mice. In short, 5 µL of U87 MG cell suspension was injected into the right caudate nucleus of the anesthetized mice. After establishing the glioma model for 2-3 weeks, T2-weighted MR images were performed. The number of mice samples in control and glioma model was 5, respectively. For the samples of ex vivo THz imaging, the mice were directly euthanized and their entire brains were removed immediately. The freshly excised brain tissues were quickly put into -15℃ microtome (Leica, CM1950) and the thin section with 10 µm thickness was sliced from the surface for histopathological examination by H&E staining. Then, the rest brain tissues with flat surface were placed under the imaging window to obtain THz images, where the tissues were not processed by any other procedure. The obtained THz images can be well compared with the H&E-stained images.

div.head: Experimental setup
div.p: The schematic diagram of the experimental system is shown in Fig. 1. An optically pumped THz gas laser (FIRL 100, Edinburgh Instruments Ltd.) with tunable continuous THz-wave output was used in this study. The frequency of 2.52 THz (corresponding to the wavelength of 118.9 µm) was chosen with the maximum output power of 150 mW. A mechanical chopper was employed for the THz beam modulation at 50 Hz due to the responsivity of the Golay cell detector (GC-1P, Tydex Ltd.). The THz-wave was separated into two beams by wire-grid beam splitter (Micromesh Instruments, Inc.). One beam was served as the signal and the other was used as the reference, where the reference light was received directly by the Golay Cell detector (GC-1P, Tydex Ltd.). The signal beam was focused into the solid immersion lens by a off-axis parabolic reflector with the focal length of 6 inches. To enhance the imaging resolution and obtain large imaging area, a novel separated hyper-hemispherical SIL was designed, which was comprised of two optical elements including a truncated hemispherical lens and an imaging window. The truncated hemispherical lens and the imaging window were both made of high-resistivity float zone silicon (HRFZ-Si), which has high refractive index in THz range (n si =3.42 at 2.52 THz). The truncated hemispherical lens had a radius of R = 25 mm and a thickness of l = 25 mm, whereas the imaging window had a thickness of l'= R × (n 0 /n si ) = 7.3 mm and a diameter of D = 70 mm, which was much larger than the underside surface of the hemispherical lens. Thus, the total thickness of the hyper-hemispherical SIL was l + l'=32.3 mm. Considering the refractive index of biological samples was usually smaller than that of water (n = 2.05 at 2.52 THz), the theoretical critical angle of THz wave should be larger than 34.8°. Therefore, the incident angle of THz wave was set as 43.5°at the bottom of the imaging window to guarantee the total reflection condition well. The incident THz beam was focused at the center of the bottom surface of imaging window. The sample was placed on the sample holder and closely attached to the bottom surface of imaging window. The imaging window and the sample holder were mounted on a two-dimensional (2-D) translation stage (Sigma Koki CO., Ltd.). During the process of stage scanning, the imaging window and the bottom surface of SIL were always parallel and closely attached to each other. The optical path of the incident THz beam and the reflected THz beam remained unchanged, which can effectively avoid the resolution degradation [13]. The scanning speed was about 10 pixels/s. The experimental temperature was kept at room temperature (23 °C).

div.head: Data analysis
div.p: In order to reduce the image noises from slight power fluctuations, THz wave was split into two beams with basically the same intensity by the beam splitter. The pixel intensity of the reference beam is named as I reference , whereas the pixel intensity of signal beam with sample information is named as I sample . 2-D image of sample was obtained with the pixel value of I sample / I reference . THz imaging with and without sample were measured as the images of F sample and F substrate , respectively. Considering the uniformity of the imaging window, the reflectivity (R) of samples can be calculated by dividing the pixel values in F substrate by F sample .

div.head: Assessment methodology
div.p: The validity assessment of THz biological imaging is an important part for clinical diagnosis. However, there are only few researches on the automatic identification of lesion areas in THz biological images. A hybrid algorithm based on the region of interest segmentation used to be developed for the automatic identification of glioma region in CW THz reflection images [25]. However, limited by the spatial resolution and contrast of the THz reflection imaging system, the identification accuracy of this algorithm was relatively low. Here, the image segmentation algorithm based on Chan-Vese active contour model was adopted for the recognition and segmentation of specific region in THz images. The Chan-Vese active contour model is a classic region-based active contour model, which adopts the difference in image grayscale means of regions inside and outside the active contour to drive the motion of the active contour toward the target boundary. It can effectively segment images with weak and discontinuous boundaries [26]. To evaluate the performance of THz image with the Chan-Vese active contour model, five evaluation parameters including accuracy (AC), precision (PR), sensitivity (SE), specificity (SP), and F1-score are calculated. The accuracy is the probability of all pixels being correcting identified. The precision is the proportion of pixels that truly belong to the glioma region among the pixels identified as glioma region. The sensitivity is defined as the rate of pixels in the glioma region being correctly identified. The specificity is the rate of pixels in normal regions being correctly identified. The F1-score is the harmonic mean of precision and sensitivity, which can reflect the overall performance of the algorithm. The five parameters were defined as follows:
div.formula: Accuracy(AC) = TP + TN TN + TP + FP + FN (1)
Specificity(SP) = TN TN + FP (4) F1 -score = 2 × PR × SE PR + SE (5)
div.p: Here, the true positive (TP) represents the correctly recognized pixels of the glioma region, the true negative (TN) represents the pixels of the non-glioma region that are recognized correctly, the false positive (FP) represents the pixels incorrectly identified as the glioma region, and the false negative (FN) represents the pixels of the glioma region that are recognized incorrectly. These parameters can form the confusion matrix to evaluate the effectiveness and performance of the segmentation algorithm comprehensively.

div.head: Theoretical analysis
div.p: According to Abbe's equation l = 0.61λ/NA = 1.22λ/2n sin θ, the system resolution l is related to the wavelength λ, the refractive index n and the entrance pupil aperture angle θ, where the refractive index n depends on the material of the object space. For the hemispherical SIL, the incident convergent THz beam propagated along the radial direction and was focused at the center of the bottom surface. Thus, the aperture angle θ had no change during the propagation process. The spatial resolution can be improved by n si times by increasing the refractive index of object space of the hemispherical SIL. For the hyper-hemispherical SIL, the incident convergent THz beam was refracted and finally focused at the center of the bottom surface, where the sine value of the aperture angle θ at the focal plane was n si times of the sine value of the aperture angle θ' under the situation of no hyper-hemispherical SIL. The numerical aperture (NA) for hyper-hemispherical SIL was n si • sin θ = n si • n si • sin θ ′ . Therefore, the spatial resolution can be improved by n si 2 times by increasing the refractive index of object space and changing the aperture angle θ for the hyper-hemispherical SIL. Figure 2 shows the relationship between the entrance pupil aperture angle θ and the normalized resolution l/λ under the situations of free space, hemispherical SIL, and hyper-hemispherical SIL, respectively. The refractive index n was set to 1 and 3.42 for the object space of free space and SIL made by HRFZ-Si, respectively. It can be seen that the normalized resolution monotonically decreased with the increasing of entrance pupil aperture angle θ under three situations. The hyper-hemispherical SIL can provide the higher resolution enhancement than that of hemispherical SIL. While the aperture angle θ was increased, the resolution enhancement ratio was gradually decreased. When there was θ<20°, the resolution enhancement of hyper-hemispherical SIL was close to n si 2 . When there was θ>60°, the resolution enhancement of hyper-hemispherical SIL became close to that of the hemispherical SIL. Therefore, it can be concluded that the n si 2 times resolution enhancement can only be achieved under the aperture value less than 20°. Then, the finite-element frequency-domain method within the COMSOL Multiphysics software was applied to numerically analyze the dimension of focus point in the THz imaging system with and without SIL, where the full-wave 2D simulation was adopted to take into account all the main features of the electromagnetic-wave-lens interaction. The lenses were illuminated with a spherical wave of homogeneous intensity distribution over the aperture. The perfectly matched layers (PMLs) were positioned at the computational cell extremities and the mesh with the subwavelength maximal element size <<λ/n si was used. The relationship between the incident angle φ' in free space and the incident angle φ in the hyper-hemispherical SIL was n si •sin φ'=sin φ. Therefore, the incident angle in free space and in hyper-hemispherical SIL was set as 11.6°a nd 43.5°, respectively. In Fig. 3(a) and (b), the field intensity distributions I(r) ∝ |E(r)| 2 were calculated in free space and the hyper-hemispherical SIL respectively, where the details of I(r) distributions near the focal spot in free space and the hyper-hemispherical SIL were shown in the insets. It can be seen that the THz focal spot in free space was significantly larger than that in hyper-hemispherical SIL. Besides, the optical field intensity in hyper-hemispherical SIL was much higher than that in free space due to the smaller focal spot. Moreover, the spatial resolution was estimated from the full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of THz focal spot. As shown in Fig. 3(c), the theoretical spatial resolution under the situations of free space and hyper-hemispherical SIL was 1.19 mm and 110 µm, respectively. It means the lateral resolution with hyper-hemispherical SIL can be enhanced 10.8 times compared with that in free space. Furthermore, in order to compare the imaging performance between different imaging modes in hyper-hemispherical SIL, the relationship between the image contrast and refractive index n 2 of sample was analyzed theoretically in reflection and ATR mode. The image contrast was calculated by the formula C = (R rsM -R rsm )/R rsM , where R rsM and R rsm represented the maximum and minimum values of THz reflectivity and were calculated based on Fresnel's equations [27]. The incident angles inside the hyper-hemispherical SIL were set as 30°for reflection mode and 43.5° for ATR mode, respectively. The relationship between image contrast and the refractive index n 2 of sample was calculated as shown in Fig. 3(d), where the refractive index n 2 was set as [1,3]. It can be indicated that the image contrast in ATR mode was significantly higher than that in reflection mode. Moreover, the contrast difference between the two imaging modes became more significant as the refractive index n 2 increased. It can be attributed to the enhanced evanescent field coupling in ATR mode, which can lead to stronger interaction with the sample. Since the image contrast was proportional to the imaging sensitivity, it can be demonstrated that the image with ATR mode can provide higher sensitivity than that with reflection mode. During the scanning imaging process, although the bottom surface of truncated hemispherical lens and the imaging window were always parallel and closely attached to each other, there was still a small air gap between them, as shown in the inset of Fig. 4. The transmittance of THz wave for hyper-hemispherical SIL is defined by the ratio of the transmitted power in imaging window I 1 (λ) to the incident power I 0 (λ) in truncated hemispherical lens. According to the optical tunneling effect [28], the THz transmittance T is dependent on the thickness of the air gap, which can be given by Eq. ( 6), (7). Here, d is the thickness of air gap, and φ represents the incident angle. The parameters α and β in Eq. ( 6) can be given by Eq. ( 8)-( 11) for s-and p-polarizations.
div.formula: T = 1 αsin h 2 y + β (6) y = 2π n 2 d λ (n si /n 2 )sin 2 φ -1(7)
α s = ((n si /n 2 ) 2 -1)((n 3 /n si ) 2 (n si /n 2 ) 2 -1) 4(n si /n 2 ) 2 cos φ((n si /n 2 ) 2 sin 2 φ -1) (n 3 /n si ) 2 -sin 2 φ(8)
β s = ( (n 3 /n si ) 2 -sin 2 φ + cos φ) 2 4 cos φ (n 3 /n si ) 2 -sin 2 φ (9
β p = ( (n 3 /n si ) 2 -sin 2 φ + (n 3 /n si ) 2 cos φ) 2 4(n 3 /n si ) 2 cos φ (n 3 /n si ) 2 -sin 2 φ(11)
div.p: The refractive indices n si , n 2 , n 3 in Eq. ( 8)-( 11) corresponded to the refractive index of SIL, air gap, and the imaging window, respectively. Considering the material of SIL and the imaging window was the same in our experiment, the relative refractive index can be expressed as n 3 /n si =1. The refractive index of air gap n 2 was the same as that of air (n 2 = n 0 = 1). On the basis, the relationship between the transmittance T and the relative thickness d/λ under different THz polarization states were theoretically analyzed, where φ was set to 43.5°to satisfy the total reflection condition. As shown in Fig. 4, when the air gap was close to 0, the maximum THz transmittance can be up to 100%. The THz transmittance was decreased gradually with the increase of the thickness of air gap. Although the changing trend of THz transmittance with the thickness of air gap was similar for different polarizations of the incident THz wave, the THz transmittance of s-polarization THz wave changed more rapidly. In other words, the THz transmittance of p-polarization THz wave was higher than that of s-polarization THz wave for the same thickness of air gap. It should be noticed that the THz transmittance can exceed 80% when the thickness of air gap was less than 0.034λ for p-polarization THz wave. As for s-polarization THz wave, the thickness should be less than 0.015λ to keep the THz transmittance more than 80%. Since p-polarization can contribute to enhanced image contrast and more stable intensity of the attenuated total internal reflected signal in THz ATR imaging system [29], p-polarization was adopted in the experiment. By adopting fine polished surface and exerting tight pressure on imaging window to reduce the thickness of air gap, the high transmittance of THz imaging system can be obtained with higher SNR.

div.head: Results and discussion
div.p: The spatial resolution of the imaging system was estimated by measuring a piece of rectangular blood agar with the scanning step of 20 µm, which was placed at the center of the bottom of the imaging window. Figure 5 showed the normalized reflectivity along x direction and y direction, which were marked by the white dashed line in the inset of Fig. 5. Based on the 10%∼90% criterion of the normalized reflectivity, the resolution of the imaging system along x direction and y direction can be up to 120 µm and 140 µm, respectively. The experimental measurement results were basically consistent with the calculation result above. In order to verify that the THz SIL-ATR imaging system has high sensitivity and high stability during large-area imaging, water droplets of different sizes were imaged. Figure 6(a) and (b) showed the visible image and THz image of the water droplets, respectively. The total THz imaging area was 25.5 × 23.0 mm 2 , which contained four water droplets of different sizes. The color bar on the right side in Fig. 6(b) indicated the reflectivity (R), where lower THz reflectivity represented higher THz absorption. As shown in Fig. 6(b), the blue region was the water droplet with high THz absorption, where the size and the position of the water droplets corresponded well with those in the visible image shown in Fig. 6(a). The average THz reflectivity of water droplets in THz image was 26.2% with a standard deviation of 0.83%. It can be indicated that the imaging system was performed with high stability during large-area scanning. Furthermore, the water droplets were imaged in reflection mode, where the system imaging mode was switched to reflection mode rapidly by rotating the off-axis parabolic mirror 1. Figure 6(c) showed the THz reflectivity in reflection and ATR imaging mode, respectively. In order to analyze the imaging sensitivity in different modes quantitatively, the image contrasts of the THz images in different imaging modes were calculated. The image contrasts of water droplet in reflection and ATR modes were 0.64 and 0.73, respectively. Considering the refractive index of water at 2.52THz is 2.05, the theoretical contrasts were 0.61 and 0.76 in reflection and ATR modes, respectively. It means the experimental results were basically consistent with the calculation results. In other words, the image contrast in ATR mode was higher than that in reflection mode for water droplet. Since the refractive indices of biosamples are usually larger than 2 in THz range, it can be demonstrated that the ATR mode can provide high sensitivity, especially under higher THz frequency. Then, the THz SIL-ATR imaging was performed on freshly excised normal mouse brain tissues. The visible image and THz image of the sagittal section of normal mice brain tissue were shown in Fig. 7(a) and (b). Notably, the structures in hippocampus and lobule of cerebellar vermis annotated in the visible image can be accurately identified in THz image. For the vertical white dashed line in Fig. 7(b), it passed through normal brain tissue, field cornu ammonis (CA) of hippocampus and molecular layer of hippocampus in turn. The detailed profile of THz reflectivity along vertical line was shown in Fig. 7(c). It can be observed that the THz reflectivity of normal brain tissue was 22.35 ± 1.78%, while the average reflectivity of molecular layer of hippocampus was 25.84 ± 1.54%. The THz reflectivity of field CA of hippocampus was 33.11 ± 1.43%, which was significantly higher than that of the normal brain tissue and molecular layer of hippocampus. It can be attributed to the lower content of tissue water, myelin, and cell density in the field CA of hippocampus, which can cause lower absorption of THz wave [30][31][32]. For the horizontal white dashed line in Fig. 7(b), it passed through normal brain tissue, field CA of hippocampus, lobule 3 of cerebella vermis (3Cb), lobule 4/5 of cerebella vermis (4/5Cb) and lobule 6 of cerebella vermis (6Cb) in turn. The detailed profile of THz reflectivity along horizontal line was shown in Fig. 7(d). The average THz reflectivities of the lobule 3, lobule 4/5 and lobule 6 of cerebellar vermis were 29.96 ± 1.30%, 31.47%±1.52%, and 32.74%±1.67%, respectively. It can be indicated that lobule 6 of cerebellar vermis had the highest reflectivity among three different lobules of cerebellar vermis. The average reflectivity of the lobule of cerebellar vermis was higher than that of normal brain tissue, but lower than that of the field CA of hippocampus. It means the constituents of these kinds of lobules of cerebellar vermis are different. Thus, the heterogeneity of brain tissues can be characterized by the high-resolution THz SIL-ATR imaging system.

In order to realize the precise discrimination of glioma boundary, the freshly excised brain glioma tissue in mice model was studied based on such high-resolution THz SIL-ATR imaging system. Figure 8 showed the visible, MR, H&E-stained, and THz ATR images for brain glioma tissues, where the glioma regions were marked by white dashed lines in Fig. 8(a) and (b). The T2-weighted MR imaging was used to observe the condition of glioma in vivo in mice. In MR images, the glioma regions were recognized as highlighted regions, indicating that the water content in the glioma tissue was higher than that in normal brain tissues [33]. After the MR scanning, the brain tissue was extracted to obtain THz ATR images. To verify the accuracy of THz ATR image, the mice with glioma were pathologically determined with H&E-stained images as references, as shown in Fig. 8(c). In H&E-stained images, the glioma regions were identified by deep purple hematoxylin staining, where the cell nuclear density of glioma tissues was higher than that of normal tissues [34]. In THz ATR images, the glioma regions with lower THz reflectivity can be clearly distinguished from normal tissues as shown in Fig. 8(d). By comparing Fig. 8(d) with Fig. 8(a)-(c), it can be demonstrated that the locations of the glioma region shown in THz ATR images correspond well to those in visible images, MR images, and H&E-stained images. Furthermore, it can be clearly seen that the normal tissues in THz ATR image were uniform with the average THz reflectivity of 32 ± 2.57%, whereas the THz reflectivity of glioma tissues was 21.21 ± 1.89%. It can be attributed to the increased water content and cell density in glioma tissues [35].

To further estimate the accuracy and effectiveness of THz ATR imaging in glioma detection, a segmentation algorithm based on the Chan-Vese active contour model was adopted in THz image to identify the target region automatically. Firstly, the noise reduction and contrast enhancement was applied to the original THz ATR images to emphasize glioma-related image details. Then, the enhanced images were converted into grayscale to provide an optimized input for contour evolution. On the basis, the Chan-Vese active contour model adopted the difference in mean grayscale values between regions inside and outside the evolving contour to drive the motion toward the glioma boundary, so that the glioma region can be identified automatically. The H&E-stained images, regarded as the gold standard in pathology, were selected as the ground truth to evaluate the performance of segmentation algorithm. The H&E-stained images were converted to grayscale and then transformed into the HSV color space to enhance image contrast.

Considering the gray-level difference between glioma and normal brain tissues, the glioma regions in H&E-stained images were identified using the Otsu adaptive thresholding method. The glioma regions in H&E-stained images and THz ATR images were identified and delineated by red and blue lines respectively in Fig. 8(c) and (d), respectively. In order to better compare the THz image and H&E-stained image, the processing of binarization of the THz ATR images was performed, where the glioma regions and normal regions in THz ATR images were presented as black and white areas, respectively. To ensure spatial correspondence between H&E-stained images and THz ATR images, a feature-based registration method was adopted to estimate and optimize the rotation, translation, and scaling parameters of H&E-stained images. Then, the registered H&E-stained images were geometrically aligned to the THz ATR images coordinate system. Subsequently, the contour of glioma region in H&E-stained images marked by red line was superimposed on the binarized THz ATR images, as shown in Fig. 8(e). It can be clearly seen that both the locations and volumes of glioma regions in THz ATR images corresponded well with those in H&E-stained images.

The confusion matrix composed of TP, TN, FP, and FN was calculated and summarized in Table 1, where the TP and TN were 95.52% and 95.02%, respectively. Furthermore, the evaluation parameters of this segmentation algorithm were calculated based on the Eq. ( 1)-( 5) listed in Section 2.4. The average accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score were 95.25%, 95.47%, 95.04%, 95.45%, and 95.26%, respectively. These results indicated that the segmentation algorithm can identify the glioma regions from normal brain tissue in THz ATR images effectively.

Besides, the segmented glioma regions in THz ATR images and H&E-stained images were calculated and listed in Table 2. The result showed that the glioma areas in THz ATR images were slightly larger than those in H&E-stained images. Since THz wave is sensitive to the distribution of water content and cellular hydration state, THz imaging could indicate the presence of perifocal edema around glioma region, which resulted in larger glioma area in THz images than those in H&E-stained images [12]. The difference between glioma area in THz ATR images and in H&E-stained images was less than 0.45 mm 2 , which is much smaller than that in previous research [12]. It should be related to the improvement of spatial resolution thereby effectively enhancing the imaging accuracy and sensitivity for lesion regions. Especially, the high-resolution THz ATR image can accurately identify glioma region with the minimum area of about 6.23 mm 2 .

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: In this work, a novel arrangement of the CW THz ATR imaging system based on SIL with high resolution and large imaging area was proposed, where the SIL was comprised of a truncated hemispherical lens and an imaging window. The imaging resolution improvement of hyper-hemispherical SIL was analyzed by finite-element frequency-domain method. And the influence of air gap thickness between the truncated hemispherical lens and imaging window on the THz transmittance under different polarization was analyzed theoretically. The THz SIL-ATR imaging system with the resolution of 120 × 140 µm can realize large area imaging. Furthermore, THz ATR imaging of freshly excised normal and glioma mice brain tissues was performed. The various microscopic structures such as hippocampus and lobule of cerebellar vermis in normal mice brain tissues can be accurately identified for their different reflectivity of THz wave. The glioma regions in THz ATR images can be well corresponded to the H&E-stained images using the automatic segmentation method based on Chan-Vese active contour model, where the average accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score were up to 95.25%, 95.47%, 95.04%, 95.45%, and 95.26%. The results indicated that THz ATR imaging based on SIL has great potential as an alternative method for the intraoperative label-free diagnosis of brain tumors.
